targetAudience.primary: Agent-runtime, automation and digital-employee engineers designing long-running monitoring work
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands scheduled jobs, polling, agent tool loops and basic event-driven systems.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Long-running monitors are often implemented as repeated agent turns or fixed polling, which entangles waiting, reasoning, cost and completion semantics.

whyNow: SentinelBench provides a newly released primary benchmark, open-source environments and same-model baselines that make waiting behavior, false-positive completion, reaction time and resource cost directly measurable.

externalHook.description: For some agent jobs, the correct next action is to do nothing until the world changes; forcing continuous action can spend more while completing less.

coreProposition: Waiting should be represented as durable runtime state with explicit condition, observation, admission and effect-evidence boundaries, rather than as repeated free-form agent turns.

originalValue.description: Derives a four-boundary monitoring correctness envelope from SentinelBench's task design and baseline evidence, separating condition state, observation policy, condition admission and external effect evidence.

readerTakeaway: Keep the monitored condition and its baseline outside the model turn, make observation policy swappable and budgeted, require evidence to admit a condition, and verify the resulting notification or action separately.

supported: SentinelBench contains 100 tasks across 10 synthetic time-evolving web environments and explicitly includes no-op, active/passive and absolute/relative task dimensions.
The benchmark evaluates resulting database state plus timing rather than relying on plausible agent output alone.
The authors report substantial cost and completion differences between wait_for and sleep under the same GPT-5.4 model, especially when task duration is stretched.
The reported reaction-time results are mixed, preserving a latency-cost tradeoff rather than a universal win.
The released wait_for prototype keeps condition and timeout explicit while managing page diffing, LLM checks, reload and backoff outside the main agent loop.
unsupported: Production reliability of SentinelBench's wait_for implementation
Reliability on subjective or ephemeral conditions
Independent reproduction of the complete reported baseline
uncertain: Best observation mechanism for production workloads
How to allocate latency and cost budgets across many concurrent monitors
How to benchmark provider-native event streams and webhooks under the same contract

firstPartyRole.rationale: The analysis concerns a general monitoring-runtime architecture and does not require a first-party project mapping.

decisionReason: The primary paper, released benchmark implementation and baseline results provide concrete mechanism-level evidence, while the Research Center adds a bounded production-oriented monitoring correctness model beyond source restatement.
